name: sg-rainglass
summary: Full-bleed hero running shader.gallery's rainglass: rain on a window at night. Behind a fogged pane a dark street of defocused lights glows in soft bokeh discs; on the glass, runners fall in wiggling stalls and darts, leaving beaded trails and wiped streaks where the lights come back into focus, while small beads swell and vanish as a runner passes. Every drop is a lens showing the lit field sharp and inverted, with a dark rim and one tight highlight.

colors.description: Four poles. These are the street lights behind the pane, and they are the whole composition: every bokeh disc and every drop-lens is one of them. Spread them apart to read as a street, cluster them to get a flat wash. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette.

rain.description: How much water is on the glass; low is a few stray drops, high is a pane streaming with runners. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.5.

speed.description: Fall speed of the runners and the swell of the beads; 0 freezes the rain. Upstream default, range 0 to 3.

smear.description: How far each drop draws its tail out behind it as it runs; 0 keeps every drop round, high turns a darting drop into a long streak. Upstream default, range 0 to 2.

fog.description: Condensation on the pane; 0 is clear glass with the lights in focus, 1 is a heavily fogged window that only the wiped streaks see through. Upstream default, range 0 to 1.

refract.description: How strongly each drop bends the field behind it; 0 makes the drops flat, high turns each into a strong inverted lens. Upstream default, range 0 to 2.

lights.description: Density of the lights behind the glass; low is a sparse dark street, high is a dense city. Upstream default, range 0.2 to 2.

deviations.what: The four u_palette colours are ours, not upstream's `peacock` preset.
deviations.why: rainglass/meta.json declares `defaultPalette: "peacock"`, and the preset table lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor and which is not in the pinned repo. The port cannot resolve the name, so it ships four of its own and declares them. The shader's zero-fallback branch is not the answer either: paletteFor never produces zeros, so that branch is unreachable from paw-fx. Same call sg-gloam, sg-bask and sg-nebula-drift made.

deviations.what: The `speed` default is 0.3, taken from rainglass/meta.json, not the 0.5 in the shader's own comment beside `uniform float u_speed`.
deviations.why: The two pinned upstream files disagree. meta.json `params` is the block upstream's runtime actually feeds the shader, so it is the one the port follows; the comment is documentation that drifted. Same arbitration sg-suminagashi made on `draw`.

deviations.what: No post chain: upstream's poster runs grain 0.055 at size 1.6, bloom 0.18 at radius 3.5, vignette 0.2, saturation 1.05 and contrast 1.03 over the shader output.
deviations.why: The post chain lives in @shader-gallery/runtime, a package paw-fx does not vendor. Our output is the raw shader, so it will not match the upstream poster. Bloom is the one that shows most here: upstream's poster spreads every light source at radius 3.5 and ours does not, so our bokeh discs and drop highlights have harder edges than the poster's soft glow.

deviations.what: Rendered through paw-fx's own WebGL runtime (effects/_shared/glsl-mount.js) rather than @shader-gallery/runtime.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream ships the .frag with no module around it. The GLSL itself is byte-identical to upstream and lives in shader.frag beside index.js.
